Introduction

Purpose and audience

This document describes the architecture of PulseAnalytics: what it is built from, how those parts fit together, and — most importantly — why each significant decision was taken and what it cost.

It is written for four readers. An engineer joining the team should be able to locate any behaviour from the component and logical views. A data analyst should be able to trust a number by tracing it from the dashboard back through the marts to the source. An architecture reviewer should be able to challenge the decisions in section 11 on their stated trade-offs. An operator should be able to reason about failure from the process and deployment views.

On the tone of this document Sections that record a decision also record what was given up to get it, and what would have to change for the decision to be revisited. An architecture document that lists only benefits is a sales document.

Scope

In scope: the ingestion, warehousing, analytical and presentation components of PulseAnalytics; its data model; its runtime and deployment topologies; and the delivery pipeline that puts it into an environment.

Out of scope: the internals of the source systems that feed it; the commercial content of the analyses themselves (covered by the companion BRD); and the Power BI report layouts, which are specified as text in dashboards/powerbi/.

Definitions

Terms used throughout this document
TermMeaning in this system
MedallionThe bronze → silver → gold layering. Bronze lands raw, silver cleans and conforms, gold serves.
GrainWhat one row of a fact table represents. Stated explicitly for all five facts in section 7.3.
Conformed dimensionA dimension shared by more than one fact, so measures from different facts can be compared along it.
Unknown memberThe -1 row present in every dimension, so a fact never loses a row to a failed join.
Semi-additiveA measure that can be summed across some dimensions but not others. Stock sums across products, never across dates.
Analysis anchorgold.analysis_window.as_of_date — the latest date in the data, used as "today" by every recency metric.
Event timeWhen an event happened, as opposed to when it was processed. All streaming windows use event time.
Reconciliation checkA data-quality check that computes one number two independent ways and requires them to agree.

Project description

What the platform does

PulseAnalytics turns two years of retail trading history and a live event stream into decisions. It ingests a nightly batch extract from an order management system, four continuous event streams, and one external API; lands and cleans them through a medallion warehouse; models them as a Kimball star schema; and serves the result through five role-specific dashboards, a real-time HTTP API, a set of analytical models, and a Power BI semantic model.

The system is built so that it runs identically on a laptop with no infrastructure at all, on Docker with PostgreSQL and Kafka, and on Azure. Only environment variables differ. That property is not a convenience — it is the mechanism by which the local demonstration is a faithful rehearsal of production rather than a separate program that resembles it.

Architectural drivers

The architecture is shaped far more by the quality attributes below than by the functional requirements. Any competent design satisfies the functional list; these are what discriminate between designs.

Quality attribute scenarios

Quality attribute scenarios and the mechanisms that satisfy them
IDAttributeScenario and response measureArchitectural mechanism
QA-01CorrectnessAn aggregate mart drifts from the fact it is built on. The discrepancy is detected on the run that introduces it, before publication.Five reconciliation checks compute revenue two independent ways; a mismatch beyond 0.01% fails the run with exit code 2.
QA-02ReproducibilityA figure quoted in March is re-derived in September from the same dataset. It matches exactly.Seeded generation; all recency metrics anchored to analysis_window.as_of_date, never the wall clock; deterministic model seeds.
QA-03PortabilityThe warehouse moves from DuckDB to PostgreSQL. No transformation logic changes.SQL restricted to the portable subset; a single dialect-adaptation point in Database._adapt; CI builds the whole warehouse on PostgreSQL every push.
QA-04ObservabilityA stage fails overnight. The operator can identify which stage, how long it ran, how many rows it moved and what the error was, without reading a terminal.ops.pipeline_runs written per stage; ops.data_quality_results per check; both surfaced on the Operations dashboard and the API.
QA-05ResilienceThe external FX endpoint is unreachable. The pipeline completes and the substitution is visible to consumers.Deterministic fallback curve; every row stamped source='fallback'; the dashboard displays the source alongside the rate.
QA-06DurabilityThe stream consumer crashes mid-batch. No event is lost.Offsets committed only after a successful write (at-least-once); event_id retained for downstream de-duplication.
QA-07RecoverabilityA production release is found to be faulty. The previous version is restored in minutes.Every deployable tagged with its git SHA and retained in the registry; rollback is a redeploy, not a rebuild.
QA-08ModifiabilityA metric definition changes. Every surface that quotes it changes together.One definition per metric, in SQL; Python and DAX consume the marts; CI asserts documented metrics exist in the SQL.
QA-09TestabilityA change to a mart breaks a downstream assumption. It fails in CI, not in a meeting.223 tests against a real warehouse built from real generated data rather than mocks.
QA-10UsabilityA reader with a colour-vision deficiency reads any chart. No meaning is lost.Fixed CVD-safe categorical order, never cycled; legend always present; direction carried by glyph and sign as well as colour.

Constraints

Constraints on the design
IDConstraintConsequence for the architecture
C-01Zero-install local runThe default engine is an embedded database and the default event bus is a file. Neither Docker nor a broker may be required to exercise any capability.
C-02No heavyweight ML dependenciesModels are implemented on numpy and pandas alone. This keeps the container small and the mathematics auditable, at the cost of writing k-means and logistic regression by hand.
C-03Two-person teamOperational surface must stay small. This is the main reason no orchestrator is deployed: one linear DAG with a run log is within the team's capacity to operate; Airflow is not.
C-04Source data quality is imperfect and will stay soBronze must never reject a row; quality thresholds must encode accepted realities rather than aspirations.
C-05Attribution limited to last touchThe source records one campaign per order. Multi-touch models are reconstructed from clickstream and published side by side rather than presented as fact.

Container view

The deployable and runnable units, and the data stores between them. Each container is independently startable: the batch pipeline, the producer, the consumer, the dashboards and the API are five separate processes that communicate only through the event bus and the warehouse.

Why the consumer writes to a table rather than holding state The dashboard, the API and the consumer are three separate processes, so shared state has to be durable and queryable. Restarting the consumer must not blank the dashboard, and retaining the window's history is what lets the live page draw a trend rather than display a single number.

Component view

Figure 5.1 is a UML component diagram: it shows provided and required interfaces rather than merely which module calls which. The distinction matters here, because two of the interfaces are the seams that make the whole portability story work.

Layering and dependency rules

Dependencies point downward only. Presentation may depend on curated access; curated access may depend on the transformation layer; nothing depends upward. The cross-cutting quality and run-context components observe the layers they instrument without being depended on by them.

Logical view

Core abstractions

The runtime has a deliberately small number of abstractions. Two of them — Database and EventBus — carry the portability requirement; the rest exist to make the pipeline observable and testable.

Responsibilities of the core types
TypeResponsibility and the reason it exists
DatabaseThe single point at which SQL meets an engine. Holds the only dialect-translation logic in the system, which is why portability is a small ongoing cost rather than a rewrite.
EventBusAbstract publish/consume with committed offsets. The file implementation is not a mock — it is a durable, replayable, ordered log, which is what makes the local demonstration meaningful.
StreamConsumerMicro-batches events into the warehouse and commits offsets afterwards. Owns no metric definitions; that is what keeps "revenue" from meaning two things.
RealtimeKpiProcessorComputes the rolling window in event time and persists each computation, so the live page survives a consumer restart.
CheckOne data-quality assertion reduced to a single shape: count failing rows and total rows. That uniformity is why the runner needs no special cases and a new check is three lines of SQL.
RunContextTimes each stage and records it to ops.pipeline_runs. Deliberately swallows its own persistence errors — a broken audit table must never roll back a good data load.

Data view

Medallion layers

Layer responsibilities and the rules that apply to each
LayerGrainRules
bronzeAs the source sent itNo NOT NULL, no keys, wide types. Never rejects a row. Lineage columns on every row.
silverOne row per business entityTrimmed, typed, de-duplicated, conformed. Every repair is flagged on the row and asserted by a check.
goldStar schema and martsWhat every consumer queries. One definition per metric.
opsPlatform metadataAppend-only. Created with CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS so a full refresh cannot destroy the run log or the streaming landing zone.
Why bronze rejects nothing If the source sends garbage it is landed and counted, rather than vanishing into a filter nobody remembers writing. Every quality question about the source is then answerable from the warehouse itself. The cost is that bronze row counts exceed silver row counts, which has to be explained once to every new reader — a much smaller cost than unexplained missing revenue.

The star schema

Grain and additivity

Fact grain, additivity and the error each choice prevents
FactGrainAdditivityWhy it is modelled this way
fact_salesOne order lineFully additiveThe atomic fact. Every product, category and margin aggregate derives from it.
fact_ordersOne order headerFully additiveOrder-level measures cannot be summed from lines without double counting, and averaging lines answers a different question. Keeping both grains explicit makes average order value impossible to compute wrongly.
fact_paymentsOne payment attemptFully additiveRetaining every attempt is what allows recoverable declines to be distinguished from lost ones.
fact_inventoryOne product per weekSemi-additiveA periodic snapshot. Summing stock over weeks reports inventory the business never held — the most common inventory reporting error, prevented structurally here.
fact_customer_eventsOne clickstream eventFully additiveBehavioural facts share the star with transactional ones, so view-to-purchase questions need no cross-system join.
Semi-additivity is enforced in three places The inventory mart reads only the latest snapshot per product, so it cannot express the wrong number; a test asserts one row per product; and the DAX measure uses LASTDATE. A convention documented in one place would eventually be violated.

Azure topology

Mapping between the local and Azure topologies
LocalAzureWhat changes in the code
data/raw/*.csvADLS Gen2, container bronzePULSE_RAW_DIR
DuckDB file / postgres:16-alpinePostgreSQL Flexible Server 16POSTGRES_HOST, POSTGRES_SSLMODE
NDJSON files / RedpandaEvent Hubs (Kafka protocol)PULSE_KAFKA_BROKERS and SASL
python -m etl.pipelineDatabricks job running that modulenothing
Streamlit and FastAPI locallyTwo Container Apps from one imagenothing
Why PostgreSQL and not Azure SQL The application supports exactly two engines: DuckDB and PostgreSQL. Provisioning Azure SQL would create a database the platform cannot connect to, and the "same code runs everywhere" property would be false at the one point where it matters. This was corrected during the deployment work; the configuration previously provisioned Azure SQL while emitting PostgreSQL connection settings.

Delivery pipeline

Cross-cutting concerns

Cross-cutting concerns and their treatment
ConcernTreatment
ConfigurationOne module, pulse.config, read once at import. Every setting has a working default, so the platform runs with no configuration at all. Environment variables are the only override mechanism, which is what makes the same image work in every environment.
LoggingConsistent format, level from PULSE_LOG_LEVEL. Pipeline stages log start and duration through a context manager rather than by hand, so no stage can silently omit its timing.
Error handlingFailures propagate after being recorded. Two exceptions are deliberate: a data-quality check that raises is recorded as a failure rather than aborting the suite, and run-metadata persistence swallows its own errors.
IdempotencyThe whole pipeline is a full rebuild and can be re-run safely. The FX loader deletes the date range it is about to write. A test asserts two consecutive runs produce identical row counts.
SecretsNever in source, never in Terraform outputs, never in a committed tfvars. Connection strings are written to Key Vault by the infrastructure and read by managed identity. Deployment uses OIDC, so no long-lived credential exists to leak.
ObservabilityTwo layers: ops.* answers "what did the pipeline do", Application Insights answers "what is the platform doing now". Neither replaces the other.
AccessibilityA fixed CVD-safe categorical palette that is never cycled; a legend always present for two or more series; direction carried by glyph and sign as well as colour. Enforced by tests over the dashboard sources.

Architecture decision record

Each decision below records the alternative that was rejected and the cost of the choice. A decision with no cost was not a decision.

Architecture decisions
IDDecisionRationale, alternative rejected, and cost
ADR-01Medallion layering rather than a single transformationThree layers isolate "why is this number wrong" to one stage. Rejected: one transformation step. Cost: roughly three times the SQL, and bronze/silver row counts differ in ways that need explaining.
ADR-02Transformations in SQL; models in PythonSQL is what the warehouse executes, runs unchanged on four engines, and is readable by analysts who do not write Python. Python takes only what needs iteration or linear algebra. Cost: two languages in one pipeline.
ADR-03Two order grains (fact_sales and fact_orders)Prevents an entire class of aggregation error structurally. Rejected: deriving order measures from lines. Cost: a second fact to maintain and reconcile — which the reconciliation checks then do automatically.
ADR-04Anchor recency to the data, not the clockMakes every segment, cohort and report reproducible. Rejected: CURRENT_DATE. Cost: one extra table, and a live deployment must repoint it.
ADR-05Flags rather than filters for non-revenue ordersOperations needs cancellations and returns; revenue excludes them by flag. Rejected: deleting them in silver. Cost: every revenue query must remember the flag — mitigated by defining revenue once.
ADR-06Unknown member (-1) in every dimensionA failed join becomes a countable number instead of a silent shortfall. Cost: every dimension carries a synthetic row that must be excluded from dimension-level reporting.
ADR-07Non-zero data-quality thresholdsA suite that fires nightly on known, accepted realities gets muted, and a muted suite catches nothing. Rejected: zero tolerance everywhere. Cost: each threshold is a judgement that must be justified and reviewed.
ADR-08Event time, not wall-clock time, for stream windowsMakes the real-time layer reproducible and therefore testable. Cost: a stopped producer leaves the dashboard showing the last window rather than zero, which must be explained on the page.
ADR-09ops.* survives a full refreshA run log that does not outlive the run is not a run log, and a batch rebuild must not destroy the streaming landing zone. Cost: schema changes to ops require an explicit drop.
ADR-10No orchestratorSix linear stages and one schedule are within a two-person team's operational capacity; Airflow is a service to run and explain. Cost: no retries, no backfill, no cross-DAG dependencies. Revisit at the second schedule.
ADR-11Full rebuild rather than incremental loadEleven seconds on the demo dataset; incremental buys complexity nothing needs. Cost: does not scale past roughly one hour of rebuild. ops.load_watermarks exists for when it must.
ADR-12Models on numpy and pandas onlyAuditable mathematics, small container. Rejected: scikit-learn. Cost: k-means, logistic regression and Holt-Winters are written and tested by hand.
ADR-13Linear churn model over a gradient-boosted oneRetention teams act on why, and coefficients are part of the deliverable. Cost: slightly lower AUC than the rejected alternative.
ADR-14Publish five attribution models rather than oneNo model is correct; the spread between them is the finding. Cost: a reader must be told which one the warehouse ships, on every surface that quotes ROAS.
ADR-15Power BI model as text, no .pbix in version controlA binary that cannot be diffed or merged does not belong in git, and a stale one is worse than none. Cost: the report must be assembled by hand from model.md and measures.dax.
ADR-16PostgreSQL on Azure, not Azure SQL or SynapsePostgreSQL is what the application speaks; Synapse is right past roughly a terabyte. Cost: a future Synapse migration is a DDL change and a bulk copy — real, but not free.
ADR-17Promote one image; never rebuild for productionA rebuild produces a different artefact from the one that was verified. Cost: a second registry and a cross-environment pull permission.
ADR-18Apply a saved plan to productionA re-plan between approval and apply can pick up an unreviewed change. Cost: the plan artefact contains sensitive values and must be treated as such.

Risks and technical debt

Known risks, technical debt and planned response
IDRisk or debtSeverityResponse
R-01Incrementality is estimated by a before/after baseline proxyHighCannot separate a campaign from a seasonal upswing, and is used to argue about budget. Labelled as a proxy on every surface. A geo holdout or matched-market design is the real answer and requires marketing to agree to withhold spend.
R-02No orchestrator; no retry or backfillMediumAccepted while there is one schedule. Stage boundaries and ops.pipeline_runs are already shaped so adding Dagster is a wrapper rather than a rewrite.
R-03SCD Type 2 has the shape but one version per customerMediumThe source ships no change history, so "revenue by the tier held at purchase time" is currently unanswerable. Needs change capture at source.
R-04Alerting is provisioned but nothing routes to itMediumDeliberate: routing to a rota that does not exist is worse than not alerting. An organisational change precedes the technical one.
R-05Quality suite detects broken data, not drifted dataMediumA disappearing category or a shifted distribution passes every current check. ops.data_quality_results is the history to build profiling on.
R-06Public network access on PostgreSQL and the registryMediumMitigated by deny-by-default firewalls and enforced TLS. Private endpoints and a VNet are the next hardening step.
R-07Deploying principal holds unconstrained RBAC AdministratorMediumNeeded because Terraform creates role assignments. Constrain with a condition limiting it to the specific roles required.
R-08Metric definitions exist in three implementationsLowSQL and Python are held together by reconciliation checks; the DAX side is verified by hand. A semantic layer collapses all three — worth doing at the fourth consumer.
R-09Prod plan artefact contains sensitive valuesLowOne-day retention, private repository. No more sensitive than the state file it was planned against.

Current verification status 223 automated tests pass against a warehouse built from real generated data. 64 of 64 data-quality checks pass. The Terraform configuration validates and the workflows lint clean. No terraform plan has yet been executed against a live Azure subscription — the configuration is proven well-formed, not yet proven accepted by the Azure API.
